# SendSeven for PHP

> Unofficial. Not affiliated with or endorsed by SendSeven GmbH.

A typed PHP SDK for the [SendSeven](https://sendseven.com) messaging API: WhatsApp, SMS, email, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram, RCS and browser push, from one client.

- **Every endpoint.** All 712 operations, generated from SendSeven's OpenAPI spec and corrected where the live API differs.
- **Typed throughout, and forgiving.** Responses are readonly objects with real types; lists paginate lazily; enums stay open to new values; a field SendSeven leaves out reads as empty instead of breaking the call.
- **Webhooks done right.** The activation challenge, timestamped signatures and typed events, verified against live deliveries.
- **Safe by default.** Idempotency keys on every write, retries only where safe, and errors that say how to fix them.
- **Built for tests.** `SendSeven::fake()` scripts responses and asserts requests through the real pipeline.

```bash
composer require reshapify/sendseven
```

Requires PHP 8.3+ and any PSR-18 HTTP client (Guzzle, Symfony HttpClient…), which is found automatically. Laravel? Use [reshapify/sendseven-laravel](https://github.com/reshapify/sendseven-laravel).

## Send a message

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\SendSeven;

$sendseven = SendSeven::client(getenv('SENDSEVEN_API_TOKEN'));

$message = $sendseven->messages()->send(
    to: '+4915112345678',
    channelId: 'ch_whatsapp',
    text: 'Your order has shipped.',
);

echo $message->id;
```

Every area of the API is a method on the client: `contacts()`, `channels()`, `whatsAppTemplates()`, `conversations()`, `campaigns()`, `webhooks()` and [65 more](docs/reference/README.md). Arguments are named and typed; optional ones are left out of the request.

## Lists

```php
// One page
$page = $sendseven->contacts()->list(search: 'acme', pageSize: 50);

foreach ($page as $contact) {
    echo $contact->name;
}

// Every contact, fetching pages only as they're reached
foreach ($sendseven->contacts()->list()->lazy() as $contact) {
    // ...
}
```

## Receive webhooks

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\Webhook;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\Events\MessageReceived;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\Events\MessageStatusUpdated;

$body = file_get_contents('php://input');   // the raw body, exactly as received
$headers = getallheaders();

// SendSeven activates an endpoint only after this unsigned challenge is echoed.
if (Webhook::isVerificationChallenge($body, $headers)) {
    header('Content-Type: application/json');
    echo json_encode(Webhook::challengeResponse($body));
    return;
}

$event = Webhook::constructEvent($body, $headers, $secret);   // throws InvalidSignature

if ($event instanceof MessageReceived) {
    $from = $event->message->fromId;              // phone, or the channel's ID for the person
    $text = $event->message->text;
    $button = $event->message->buttonReply()?->id; // a tapped button, however it arrived
}

if ($event instanceof MessageStatusUpdated && $event->failed()) {
    $why = $event->message->errorCode();          // e.g. "131047": outside WhatsApp's 24 hours
}
```

See the [webhooks guide](docs/guides/webhooks.md) for every event and how SendSeven signs them.

## Let customers connect their own channels

SendSeven runs WhatsApp's Embedded Signup (and Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, SMS and email onboarding) on a hosted page. Create a link, send the customer to it, and a `channel.created` webhook tells you when they're done.

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Enums\ChannelType;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Onboarding\ConnectLink;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Onboarding\WhatsAppMode;

$link = $sendseven->connectLinks()->create(
    ConnectLink::for(ChannelType::WhatsApp)
        ->modes(whatsapp: [WhatsAppMode::Classic])
        ->brandedAs('Acme')
        ->redirectTo('https://app.acme.test/channels/connected')
        ->singleUse()
        ->expiresIn(hours: 48),
);

header('Location: '.$link->connectUrl);
```

More in [onboarding channels](docs/guides/onboarding-channels.md).

## One tenant, or many

A token belongs to one SendSeven tenant (workspace), and everything works with it on any plan that includes the API. Platforms that give each customer their own sub-account can act on it with `forTenant()`:

```php
$sendseven->forTenant($customerTenantId)->contacts()->list();
```

That needs SendSeven's **multi-tenant management** (Professional, Scale, Enterprise or API Only; not Basic, or a trial that has ended), and creating tenants needs a token from the **billing account's owner**. Check before you rely on it:

```php
$capabilities = $sendseven->capabilities();

if (! $capabilities->canCreateTenants()) {
    echo $capabilities->whyNotCreateTenants();
}
```

See [tenancy and plans](docs/guides/tenancy.md).

## Errors

Every exception implements `Reshapify\SendSeven\Exceptions\SendSevenException`, and its message names the endpoint, the status and what to do:

```
feature_disabled (POST /tenants, HTTP 403, request req_8f2…). The account's SendSeven plan doesn't
include multi_tenant: it comes with Professional, Scale, Enterprise or API Only.
```

| Exception | When |
|---|---|
| `AuthenticationFailed` | 401: the token is wrong, expired or revoked |
| `PermissionDenied` | 403: the token lacks a scope |
| `FeatureDisabled` | 403: the plan lacks a feature; `feature()` names it |
| `NotBillingAccountOwner` | 403: only the billing account's owner can create tenants |
| `NotFound` | 404 |
| `ValidationFailed` | 422; `fieldErrors()` lists each field |
| `RateLimited` | 429 after retries; `retryAfter()` |
| `InsufficientBalance` | 402 or an `insufficient_*` code, e.g. the RCS wallet |
| `ServerError` | 5xx after retries |
| `TransportFailed` | SendSeven couldn't be reached |
| `UnexpectedResponse` | a field came back with the wrong type, or the body wasn't JSON. A field that's simply missing reads as an empty value instead (`''`, `0`, `false`, `[]`), so the original is on `->raw()` |

## Retries, rate limits and idempotency

Writes get an `Idempotency-Key` automatically, so retrying them is safe; pass your own (`idempotencyKey: 'order-42-shipped'`) to make a repeat from your side safe too. 429s, 5xx and connection failures are retried up to three times with backoff, honouring `Retry-After`. A token allows 100 standard requests a minute: give processes that share it a shared `RateLimiter`. See [resilience](docs/guides/resilience.md).

```php
$sendseven = SendSeven::factory()
    ->withToken($token)
    ->withRetries(5)
    ->withRateLimiter($sharedLimiter)
    ->withHttpClient($psr18Client)
    ->make();
```

## Testing

```php
$fake = SendSeven::fake([
    'POST /messages' => ['id' => 'msg_1', 'direction' => 'outbound', 'message_type' => 'text', /* ... */],
]);

$service = new OrderNotifier($fake->client);
$service->shipped($order);

$fake->assertSent('POST /messages', fn ($request) => $request->body['to'] === '+4915112345678');
```

Webhook tests can sign their own deliveries with `Webhook::sign($body, $secret)`. See [testing](docs/guides/testing.md).

## Anything else

`$sendseven->request(Method::Get, '/some/new/endpoint')` calls any endpoint with the same authentication, retries and errors. `->raw()` on any response object returns the original JSON, including fields the SDK doesn't model.

<!-- AGENTS.md -->

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI agents using or changing this SDK. Humans are welcome too.

## Using the SDK

- **Find an endpoint** in `openapi/manifest.json`. It maps every SendSeven operation (operationId, `METHOD /path`, summary, scopes) to its call, e.g. `$sendseven->contacts()->list()`, with parameter names, types and the return type. `docs/reference/<resource>.md` has the same with examples.
- **Call with named arguments**: `->send(to: '+49…', channelId: $id, text: 'Hi')`. Optional arguments left out are omitted from the request; don't pass `null` to mean "clear".
- **Responses are typed objects.** Read properties (`$message->fromId`); `->raw()` has the original JSON. Enum properties may hold a plain string when SendSeven adds a value: compare with `=== EnumType::Case` and handle the string case.
- **Lists:** methods returning `Page<T>` iterate the page; `->lazy()` walks every page.
- **Webhooks:** always check `Webhook::isVerificationChallenge()` first and answer with `Webhook::challengeResponse()`. Then use `Webhook::constructEvent($rawBody, $headers, $secret)` with the raw body, exactly as received. Match on event classes (`MessageReceived`, `MessageStatusUpdated`, `ChannelEvent`…).
- **Tenancy:** a token is one tenant. Only use `forTenant()` and `tenants()->create()` when `$sendseven->capabilities()->canManageTenants()` or `canCreateTenants()` says so; explain `whyNotCreateTenants()` to the user otherwise.
- **Onboarding channels:** use `connectLinks()->create(ConnectLink::for(...))`. Never try to run Meta's Embedded Signup directly; SendSeven runs it on the connect page. RCS and browser push can't be connected that way (see `docs/guides/channels.md`).
- **Errors** carry a fix in their message. Catch `SendSevenException` for everything; specific classes are listed in the README.
- **Undocumented endpoint?** `$sendseven->request(Method::Post, '/path', body: [...])` keeps authentication, retries and error handling.
- **Tests:** `SendSeven::fake([...])`, then `$fake->assertSent(...)`. Sign webhook bodies with `Webhook::sign()`.

Read `docs/known-quirks.md` before trusting SendSeven's own spec on webhooks, message fields or tenancy.

## Changing the SDK

- **Never edit generated files.** Anything with `@generated by bin/generate` in its header (`src/Resources/*`, `src/Data/*`, most of `src/Enums/*`, `docs/reference/*`, `llms.txt`, `openapi/manifest.json`) is overwritten. To fix one:
  - a wrong or missing spec detail → add a patch in `openapi/patches/*.json`, with an `x-source` saying how it was verified;
  - a naming or typing problem everywhere → change `generator/src`;
  - a helper a resource needs → a hand-written trait `src/Resources/Concerns/{Resource}Helpers.php`, which the generator mixes in.

  Then run `composer generate`.
- **Hand-written code** lives in `src/Http`, `src/Exceptions`, `src/Webhooks`, `src/Onboarding`, `src/Account`, `src/Support`, `src/Testing`, `src/Pagination`, `src/Client.php`, `src/Factory.php` and `src/SendSeven.php`.
- **The bar** (`composer test` must pass):
  - Pint;
  - Rector;
  - PHPStan at max level with strict rules, with no ignores and no baseline;
  - 100% type coverage;
  - Pest, including the contract test that calls all 712 endpoints and the test that every call in the docs exists.
- **Style:**
  - `declare(strict_types=1)`, `final` classes, `readonly` value objects, named constructors;
  - no static state outside `SendSeven`;
  - docblocks only where they add types or meaning.
  - Exception messages say what happened, where, and what to do next.
- **Tests** describe behaviour (`it('retries rate limits with the same idempotency key')`). Use real captured payloads (`tests/Fixtures`) over invented ones.
- **Verify claims about SendSeven** against the live API or docs.sendseven.com, and record the source. If unsure, say so rather than guess.

<!-- docs/known-quirks.md -->

# Known quirks

Where SendSeven's live behaviour differs from its OpenAPI spec or its prose docs, and what the SDK does about it. Each entry says when and how it was verified. Generated code picks up spec corrections from `openapi/patches/`.

| What | Reality | Handled by | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| Webhook verification | The endpoint-creation challenge is **unsigned** and must be answered with `{"challenge": "..."}`, or the endpoint never activates | `Webhook::isVerificationChallenge()`, `challengeResponse()` | Live, promo-next and TradeOps, Sep 2026 |
| Webhook signature | `sha256=HMAC(secret, "{X-SendSeven-Timestamp}.{raw body}")` in `X-SendSeven-Signature`. Not a body-only HMAC, and not `X-Webhook-Signature` (sendseven.com's own guide uses that name) | `WebhookVerifier` | Live deliveries, Sep 2026; docs.sendseven.com |
| Inbound message fields | The sender is `message.from_id` and the type `message.message_type`; files are in `message.attachments[]` (`signed_url`, `url`, `content_type`) | `Webhooks\Data\Message` | Live capture (`tests/Fixtures/webhooks/live-contract.json`) |
| Failure reasons | Under `message.meta.error` and `message.meta.error_code`, not top-level fields | `Message::errorCode()`, `errorMessage()` | docs.sendseven.com, Oct 2026 |
| Button replies | Arrive as `meta.button`, a `button_reply` attachment, or `interactive.list_reply` | `Message::buttonReply()` | TradeOps payloads, Sep 2026 |
| `contact.subscribed` and `contact.unsubscribed` | List (newsletter) subscriptions, not browser push. No field-level payload is documented | Parsed as `UnknownEvent` | docs.sendseven.com, Oct 2026 |
| `POST /whatsapp-templates/translate` | Exists, but missing from the spec. Requires `body_text` and `target_language` | `openapi/patches/undocumented-endpoints.json` | Live 422, 1 Oct 2026 |
| `POST /messages/proxy` | Exists, but missing from the spec. Passes a request to the channel's platform API (e.g. WhatsApp read receipts) | Patch; `messages()->markWhatsAppMessageAsRead()` | Live 422, 1 Oct 2026 |
| RCS wallet endpoints | Documented in prose, missing from the spec | Patch (`rcsWallet()`) | docs.sendseven.com, Oct 2026 |
| `PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}` and `.../channel-priority` | The spec omits the `tenant_id` path parameter | The generator infers undeclared path parameters | Contract test, 1 Oct 2026 |
| `MessageCreate.to` | Typed as anything in the spec; it's a string address | Patch | docs.sendseven.com |
| Creating tenants | Needs the `multi_tenant` plan feature **and** a token from the billing account's owner | `FeatureDisabled`, `NotBillingAccountOwner`, `Client::capabilities()` | Live refusals, 1 Oct 2026 |
| Viber | Listed in `ChannelType`, but has no connect flow, capabilities or docs | Kept in the enum; not offered by `ConnectLink` | docs.sendseven.com, Oct 2026 |
| Required fields | The spec's "required" lists aren't reliable (several above were wrong) | Missing fields read as empty values; wrong types still throw | Design decision, 1 Oct 2026 |
| RCS availability | Germany only, for accounts billed in DE; provisioned by SendSeven, not through connect links | `ConnectLink::for()` refuses RCS with an explanation | docs.sendseven.com, Oct 2026 |

Found another? Add a patch with an `x-source` saying how you verified it, regenerate, and add a row here.

<!-- docs/guides/channels.md -->

# Channels and identifiers

## Addressing people

| Channel | `to` is | Can you message first? |
|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp | Phone number (E.164) | Templates anytime; free text within 24 hours of their last message |
| SMS | Phone number (E.164) | Yes, in the countries you allow |
| RCS | Phone number (E.164) | Yes, to opted-in contacts; no window |
| Email | Email address | Yes |
| Telegram | Chat ID, scoped to **your** bot | Only after they've started your bot |
| Messenger | Page-scoped ID (PSID) | Within 24 hours of their last message |
| Instagram | IG-scoped ID | Within 24 hours of their last message |
| Browser push | — (a subscription) | Anytime, once they've allowed notifications |

Telegram, Messenger and Instagram IDs **only exist once the person messages you**, and only for your bot, Page or account. An ID from another system is meaningless, so they can't be imported. Grow these channels with links that start a conversation (`t.me/<bot>?start=...`, `m.me/<page>?ref=...`); see `lists()->getSignupOptions()`.

You can also send by contact instead of address: `messages()->send(contactId: ..., channelId: ...)` or `contactMethodId:`, and SendSeven resolves the address.

## Reply windows

`ChannelType::replyWindowHours()` gives 24 for WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram, and null for the rest.

- **WhatsApp:** outside the window, only approved templates (`whatsAppTemplates()->send()`) are accepted. A free-form message fails with error `131047`.
- **Messenger and Instagram:** outside the window, sends are refused. Meta's Human Agent tag extends replies by a person (not automation) to 7 days, subject to Meta's review. Other message tags were retired in 2026.

## Limits that matter

| Channel | Text limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp | 4,096 | Captions 1,024; up to 3 reply buttons, lists 10×10 |
| Telegram | 4,096 | Up to 8 inline buttons |
| Messenger | 2,000 | Up to 3 buttons, 13 quick replies; no documents |
| Instagram | 1,000 | Quick replies; no documents or audio |
| RCS | 3,072 | Up to 11 suggestions; rich cards and carousels |
| SMS | — | Text only; long messages bill as several segments |

SendSeven splits over-length text into ordered messages instead of failing. `channels()->getCapabilities($channelId)` and `getFileSupport()` give the live limits for a channel.

## RCS

- Available **only in Germany**, to accounts whose billing country is DE (exceptions on request to SendSeven).
- SendSeven sets up each RCS agent after Google and the carriers verify the business. Connect links can't create one.
- Paid from a separate prepaid **RCS wallet** (first top-up at least EUR 100 net), charged per delivered message: `basic` (plain text of 160 characters or fewer), `single` (anything else; EUR 0.079 net by default), `session`, or `mau` for newsletter agents (EUR 0.19 per recipient per month). Each per-message send also counts as a SendSeven message. Your prices: `rcsWallet()->getPrices()`.
- No automatic SMS fallback: a phone that can't receive RCS fails with `rcs_not_reachable` and isn't charged.
- Insufficient balance throws `InsufficientBalance` (`insufficient_rcs_balance`).

## Pricing

SendSeven charges one per-message rate on every channel, which depends on the plan (EUR 0.005 on API Only at the time of writing). SMS adds the carrier cost per segment (`sms()->pricelist()` and `sms()->priceMessage()`). Meta bills WhatsApp conversation fees directly. Inbound messages are free, and reactions are never billed.

<!-- docs/guides/onboarding-channels.md -->

# Onboarding channels

Most platforms built on SendSeven need their customers to connect their own WhatsApp number, Facebook Page, Instagram account or Telegram bot. SendSeven handles the provider flows (including Meta's **Embedded Signup** for WhatsApp) on a hosted, white-label page. You create a link, send the customer there, and they come back connected.

There is no public API for running Meta's Embedded Signup yourself; connect links are how SendSeven exposes it.

## Create a link

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Enums\ChannelType;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Onboarding\ConnectLink;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Onboarding\WhatsAppMode;

$link = $sendseven->connectLinks()->create(
    ConnectLink::for(ChannelType::WhatsApp)
        ->modes(whatsapp: [WhatsAppMode::Classic]) // hide Coexistence
        ->brandedAs('Acme')                         // shown on the connect page
        ->redirectTo('https://app.acme.test/channels/connected')
        ->named('Customer 1042')                    // your own label
        ->singleUse()                               // 1 connection
        ->expiresIn(hours: 48),                     // 1–168, default 24
);

$link->id;          // keep it: channel.created carries it back
$link->connectUrl;  // send the customer here
```

For a platform with a sub-account per customer, create the link in their tenant so the channel lands there:

```php
$sendseven->forTenant($customerTenantId)->connectLinks()->create($link);
```

## What can be connected

`ConnectLink::for()` accepts WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Messenger and SMS, and the email providers as strings: `gmail`, `smtp_imap`, `sendgrid_byok`, `mailgun_byok` and `sendgrid_managed`.

Two channels are set up differently:

- **RCS** is provisioned by SendSeven itself after Google and the carriers verify the business. It's available only in Germany, to accounts billed there. See [channels](channels.md).
- **Browser push** comes from a website widget with push enabled (`widgets()->create(config: ['pushEnabled' => true, ...])`), installed with `widgets()->getEmbedCode()`.

## Connect modes

Some channels connect in more than one way:

| Channel | Modes |
|---|---|
| WhatsApp | `Classic` (Cloud API through Embedded Signup), `Coexistence` (the number keeps working in the WhatsApp Business app too) |
| Instagram | `Messaging` (DMs), `Social` (comments) |
| Messenger | `BusinessMessaging`, `BusinessSocial`, `PersonalSocial` |

Leave modes out to allow everything the account's plan supports. Modes only ever narrow the choice: a link can't unlock a mode the account doesn't have, and the connect page shows only what's actually allowed.

## When the customer isn't the Meta admin

The person setting things up often isn't an admin of the Meta Business portfolio that owns the number or Page. Email the link to whoever is:

```php
$sendseven->connectLinks()->delegate(
    email: 'it@customer.test',
    channelTypes: ['whatsapp'],
    recipientName: 'Sam',
    note: 'Please connect our WhatsApp number for Acme notifications.',
);
```

Delegated links are deliberately tight: two uses (one attempt plus one retry), a 60-minute window after first use, and one platform. The response always includes `connectUrl`, even if the email fails.

## Knowing when it's done

Subscribe to `channel.created`. Its channel carries the link that created it:

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\Events\ChannelEvent;

if ($event instanceof ChannelEvent && $event->wasConnectedVia($customer->connect_link_id)) {
    $customer->update(['sendseven_channel_id' => $event->channel->id]);
}
```

This beats syncing `channels()->list()` when the customer is redirected back: the webhook arrives even if they close the tab.

## Managing links

```php
$sendseven->connectLinks()->listTokens(includeExpired: false);
$sendseven->connectLinks()->getToken($id);
$sendseven->connectLinks()->getTokenAuditLogs($id);   // who opened it, what they connected
$sendseven->connectLinks()->revokeToken($id);
```

For WhatsApp numbers connected with Coexistence, check the sync state with `whatsApp()->getCoexistenceStatus($channelId)`.

<!-- docs/guides/resilience.md -->

# Rate limits, retries and idempotency

## Idempotency

Every POST and PATCH gets an `Idempotency-Key` header automatically. If a retry repeats the request, SendSeven answers with the first result instead of acting twice.

Pass your own key when *your* code might repeat the call, for example a queued job that can run twice:

```php
$sendseven->messages()->send(
    to: $order->phone,
    channelId: $channelId,
    text: "Order {$order->number} shipped.",
    idempotencyKey: "order-{$order->id}-shipped",
);
```

Reusing a key with a different body is refused with `Conflict`.

## Retries

| Situation | Retried? |
|---|---|
| 429 Too Many Requests | Yes, after `Retry-After` when sent |
| 5xx | Yes, with exponential backoff and jitter |
| Connection failure, DNS, TLS, timeout | Yes |
| GET, PUT, DELETE | Always safe to retry |
| POST, PATCH | Only with an idempotency key (on by default) |
| 4xx other than 429 | Never: the request needs changing |

Three attempts by default:

```php
SendSeven::factory()->withToken($token)->withRetries(5, baseDelayMilliseconds: 250)->make();
SendSeven::factory()->withToken($token)->withoutRetries()->make();
```

Turning off automatic idempotency keys (`withoutAutomaticIdempotencyKeys()`) also stops POST and PATCH from being retried.

## Rate limits

SendSeven allows **100 standard requests a minute per token**. Everything that shares a token shares that budget: web requests, queue workers and cron jobs. Without coordination, one burst gets everyone else 429s.

Implement `Reshapify\SendSeven\Http\RateLimiter` against a shared store (Redis, a database) and pass it to the factory:

```php
interface RateLimiter
{
    public function acquire(Request $request): void;                     // before each attempt: wait, or throw
    public function observe(Request $request, Response $response): void; // learn from 429s and headers
}
```

A good limiter, as promo-next learned in production:

- keeps headroom below the limit;
- caps bulk sends (campaigns) to part of the budget, so live conversations always have capacity;
- caps each of your customers to a fair share, so one busy customer slows down alone;
- after a 429, pauses every caller until the window resets.

The Laravel package ships one backed by Laravel's cache.

## Timeouts

Configure them on your PSR-18 client (for Guzzle: `new Client(['timeout' => 20])`) and pass it with `withHttpClient()`.

<!-- docs/guides/tenancy.md -->

# Tenancy and plans

## The model

```
Billing account          (one payment relationship)
 ├── Tenant A            (a workspace: its own channels, contacts, conversations, tokens, webhooks)
 ├── Tenant B
 └── ...
```

An API token belongs to **one tenant**, and every call with it happens in that tenant. That's all most integrations need, on any SendSeven plan that includes the API.

## Two integration shapes

**Single tenant.** One token, configured once. Your channels, your contacts. This works on every plan with API access.

```php
$sendseven = SendSeven::client($token);
```

**Tenant per customer.** Platforms and agencies give each customer their own sub-account, for isolation and per-customer billing views. Create the tenant, then either store a token for it or act on it from a parent token:

```php
$tenant = $sendseven->tenants()->create(name: 'Acme', companyEmail: 'ops@acme.test');

// act on it through X-Tenant-ID
$acme = $sendseven->forTenant($tenant->id);
$acme->connectLinks()->create(/* ... */);
$acme->webhooks()->createEndpoint(/* ... */);
```

## What partner features need

| To | You need |
|---|---|
| Create tenants (`tenants()->create()`) | **Multi-tenant management** on the plan, and a token from the **billing account's owner** |
| Act on another tenant (`forTenant()`) | Multi-tenant management, and the **`tenants:manage`** grant |
| Issue a token for a tenant (`apiTokens()->create()` with `forTenant()`) | The same |

Multi-tenant management comes with **Professional, Scale, Enterprise and API Only**, but not Basic. A trial that has ended loses it.

When it's missing, SendSeven refuses with errors the SDK turns into actionable exceptions:

| SendSeven says | You get |
|---|---|
| `{"detail": {"code": "feature_disabled", "feature": "multi_tenant"}}` | `FeatureDisabled`; `feature()` is `"multi_tenant"` |
| `{"detail": "Only billing account owners can create new tenants"}` | `NotBillingAccountOwner` |

## Check first

```php
$capabilities = $sendseven->capabilities();

$capabilities->package();            // "API_ONLY", "BASIC", …
$capabilities->hasMultiTenant();
$capabilities->canCreateTenants();   // multi-tenant + tenants:create scope
$capabilities->canManageTenants();   // multi-tenant + tenants:manage
$capabilities->hasScope('messages:create');
$capabilities->sendsSms();           // SMS enabled on this tenant
$capabilities->sendsRcs();
$capabilities->whyNotCreateTenants(); // a sentence, or null
```

The API can't tell whether the token's user owns the billing account, so `canCreateTenants()` may be true and creation still fail with `NotBillingAccountOwner`.

## Webhooks per tenant

Webhook endpoints belong to a tenant. With a tenant per customer, register one endpoint per tenant (through `forTenant()`). Include the tenant in the URL (`/webhooks/sendseven/{tenant}`) so your handler can find the right secret, since each endpoint has its own.

---

<!-- docs/guides/testing.md -->

# Testing

## Fake the API

`SendSeven::fake()` returns a fake whose `client` sends nothing. It answers from a script and records every request. Requests still go through the real pipeline (headers, idempotency keys, error mapping), so a scripted 422 throws `ValidationFailed` just as SendSeven would. Retries are off, so a scripted failure fails once.

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Http\Request;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Http\Response;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\SendSeven;

$fake = SendSeven::fake([
    'POST /messages' => ['id' => 'msg_1', 'direction' => 'outbound', 'message_type' => 'text'],
    'GET /contacts/*' => ['id' => 'ct_1', /* ... */],
    'POST /tenants' => new Response(403, '{"detail":{"code":"feature_disabled","feature":"multi_tenant"}}'),
]);

$notifier = new OrderNotifier($fake->client);
$notifier->shipped($order);

$fake->assertSent('POST /messages');
$fake->assertSent('POST /messages', fn (Request $request) => $request->body['to'] === '+4915112345678');
$fake->assertNotSent('DELETE *');
$fake->assertSentCount(1, 'POST /messages');
$fake->requests(); // every Request, in order
```

**Script values** can be:
- an array, sent as JSON with status 200, or 201 for POST;
- a `Response`, for a specific status, headers or body;
- a closure that receives the `Request` and returns either of those;
- a list of any of these, used in turn, with the last one repeating.

**Patterns** are `METHOD /path`; `*` matches any run of characters, and a bare `*` matches anything.

A request with no scripted answer throws `UnexpectedRequest`, saying how to script it.

## Inject the client

Type-hint `Reshapify\SendSeven\Client` in your services and build it in one place (a container binding or factory), so tests can pass `$fake->client`.

## Test webhook handlers

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\Webhook;

$body = json_encode([
    'id' => 'evt_1',
    'type' => 'message.received',
    'data' => ['message' => ['id' => 'msg_1', 'message_type' => 'text', 'text' => 'Hi', 'from_id' => '+4915112345678', 'direction' => 'inbound']],
]);

$headers = Webhook::sign($body, 'test-secret'); // X-SendSeven-Timestamp and X-SendSeven-Signature
```

Post `$body` with those headers to your endpoint, configured with `test-secret`. Test the challenge too: post `{"type":"sendseven_verification","challenge":"abc"}` with `X-SendSeven-Event: verification` and expect `{"challenge":"abc"}` back.

## Contract tests against the real API

This repository's own suite includes opt-in live tests (`tests/Live`) that make read-only calls. Run them with a test token:

```bash
SENDSEVEN_TEST_TOKEN=s7_api_... vendor/bin/pest --group=live
```

---

<!-- docs/guides/webhooks.md -->

# Webhooks

SendSeven posts events to your endpoint: messages in, delivery updates out, channels connecting and disconnecting, contacts changing.

## Three rules

1. **Answer the challenge.** When an endpoint is created (or its URL changes), SendSeven sends one **unsigned** request and only activates the endpoint if you echo its `challenge`. A handler that rejects unsigned requests never receives a single event.
2. **Verify everything else**, using the raw body exactly as received. Parsing and re-encoding the JSON changes the bytes and breaks the signature.
3. **Acknowledge fast.** Return 2xx within 30 seconds and do slow work in a queue. Failed deliveries are retried, and an endpoint that keeps failing is suspended.

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\Webhook;
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\InvalidSignature;

if (Webhook::isVerificationChallenge($body, $headers)) {
    return json_response(Webhook::challengeResponse($body)); // {"challenge": "..."}, status 200
}

try {
    $event = Webhook::constructEvent($body, $headers, $secret);
} catch (InvalidSignature $exception) {
    return response($exception->getMessage(), 401);
}

dispatch(new HandleSendSevenEvent($event->raw())); // then return 200
```

`$headers` can be any shape frameworks give you: `['X-SendSeven-Signature' => '...']`, PSR-7 lists, or `$_SERVER` keys like `HTTP_X_SENDSEVEN_SIGNATURE`. For a PSR-7 request, use `Webhook::constructEventFromRequest($request, $secret)`.

## How SendSeven signs deliveries

```
X-SendSeven-Timestamp: 1770000000
X-SendSeven-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "1770000000.<raw body>" with the endpoint's secret>
```

- The timestamp is part of what's signed, so an old delivery can't be replayed. Deliveries more than 300 seconds from your clock are refused; change it with `toleranceSeconds:`.
- The secret is shown **once**, when the endpoint is created (`webhooks()->createEndpoint()` returns it). Store it; `regenerateSecret()` replaces it.
- If you registered the endpoint with an `authorizationHeader`, pass the same value as `authorization:` and it's checked as a second, independent gate.

The SDK's earlier relatives got this wrong twice, by signing the body alone and by reading `X-Webhook-Signature`. Both silently reject every real event. `WebhookVerifier::signature()` is the reference implementation.

## Registering an endpoint

```php
use Reshapify\SendSeven\Webhooks\EventType;

$endpoint = $sendseven->webhooks()->createEndpoint(
    name: 'My app',
    url: 'https://app.example.com/webhooks/sendseven', // HTTPS and public
    subscribedEvents: array_map(fn ($type) => $type->value, EventType::messaging()),
);

$secret = $endpoint->secretKey; // store it now
```

Your endpoint must answer the challenge immediately, so deploy the handler first. If verification failed, fix the handler and call `webhooks()->verifyEndpoint($webhookId)`.

## Events

| Event class | Types | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `MessageReceived` | `message.received` | `message`, `conversation`, `contact`, `contactMethod` |
| `MessageStatusUpdated` | `message.sent`, `.delivered`, `.read`, `.failed` | `message`; `status()`, `failed()` |
| `MessageReactionChanged` | `message.reaction` | `reaction` (`emoji`, `added`), `message` |
| `ChannelEvent` | `channel.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted` | `channel`; `change()`, `wasConnectedVia($linkId)` |
| `ContactEvent` | `contact.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted` | `contact` |
| `ConversationEvent` | `conversation.created`, `.closed`, `.assigned`, `.reopened`, `.updated` | `conversation`, `contact` |
| `UnknownEvent` | everything else (campaign, comment, post, email, link and new types) | `data` |

Every event has `id` (unique per event: use it to ignore redeliveries), `eventId` (the underlying occurrence; often the message ID), `createdAt`, `tenantId`, `type` and `raw()`.

### Messages

- `message->fromId` is the sender: a phone number on WhatsApp, SMS and RCS, or the channel's ID for the person on Telegram, Messenger and Instagram.
- `message->type` is SendSeven's `message_type`: `text`, `image`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, `sticker`, `location`, `contact`, `interactive`, `button`, `reaction`…
- `message->text` is the text, or a media caption (`""` when there is none).
- `message->attachment()` gives the first file. Use `downloadUrl()`: the signed URL needs no token but expires 24 hours after the event; `url` needs the API token and never expires.
- `message->buttonReply()` gives the button or list row tapped. SendSeven reports it in three ways (`meta.button`, a `button_reply` attachment, or `interactive.list_reply`), and this checks all three.
- `message->errorCode()` and `errorMessage()` explain a failure: Meta's codes such as `131047` (outside the 24-hour window), or SendSeven's such as `rcs_not_reachable`.
- `message->contactInfo()` holds sender details SendSeven sometimes adds: name, phone, WhatsApp username and business-scoped ID.

### Channels

`channel.created` fires when a customer finishes a connect link, so there's no need to poll:

```php
if ($event instanceof ChannelEvent && $event->wasConnectedVia($storedConnectLinkId)) {
    // the channel your customer just connected: $event->channel->id
}
```

`channel.updated` with `change() === 'status_changed'` and `! $event->channel->isConnected()` means a channel went offline; `disconnectionReason` says why (`token_invalidated`, `partner_removed`…). Prompt the customer to reconnect.

### Not what it sounds like

`contact.subscribed` and `contact.unsubscribed` are about **lists** (newsletter subscriptions), not browser notifications. SendSeven doesn't document their field-level payload, so they arrive as `UnknownEvent`.

## Testing webhook handlers

```php
$body = json_encode([...]);
$headers = Webhook::sign($body, 'test-secret'); // X-SendSeven-Timestamp and X-SendSeven-Signature

$response = $this->postJson('/webhooks/sendseven', json_decode($body, true), $headers);
```

`tests/Fixtures/webhooks/live-contract.json` in this repository holds deliveries captured from the live API, which are useful as realistic fixtures.

# AI Answers

`$sendseven->aiAnswers()` — 4 endpoints.

| Method | HTTP | Summary |
|---|---|---|

| [`listConversation()`](#listconversation) | `GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/ai-answers` | List Conversation Ai Answers |

## get

Get Ai Answer. `GET /ai-answers/{event_id}`

Get one AI answer event with its sources and rating state.

```php
$result = $sendseven->aiAnswers()->get(eventId: 'event_id');
```

- Scopes: `conversations:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$eventId` | `string` | yes |  |

Returns `AiAnswerEvent`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/AI%20Answers/get_ai_answer_api_v1_ai_answers__event_id__get)

## deleteRating

Delete Ai Answer Rating. `DELETE /ai-answers/{event_id}/rate`

Withdraw your own rating. Affected entry scores are recomputed.

```php
$result = $sendseven->aiAnswers()->deleteRating(eventId: 'event_id');
```

- Scopes: `conversations:write`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$eventId` | `string` | yes |  |

Returns `Delete`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/AI%20Answers/delete_ai_answer_rating_api_v1_ai_answers__event_id__rate_delete)

## rate

Rate Ai Answer. `POST /ai-answers/{event_id}/rate`

Rate an AI answer 👍 / 👎 / ✗ (upsert — re-rating replaces).

down and wrong REQUIRE reason_category: a verdict with no reason cannot drive the correction loop and only produces noise in the score.

```php
$result = $sendseven->aiAnswers()->rate(eventId: 'event_id', verdict: 'verdict');
```

- Scopes: `conversations:write`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$eventId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$verdict` | `string` | yes | up \| down \| wrong |
| `$reasonCategory` | `?string` | no | Required for down/wrong: factually_wrong \| outdated \| incomplete \| off_topic \| wrong_tone \| policy_violation \| hallucinated |
| `$comment` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$betterAnswer` | `?string` | no | What the answer should have said |
| `$sourceAttribution` | `list<string>\|null` | no | faq_items.id values the rater explicitly blames. Takes full weight with no sharing (ignored for 'up' verdicts). |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AiAnswerRate`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/AI%20Answers/rate_ai_answer_api_v1_ai_answers__event_id__rate_post)

## listConversation

List Conversation Ai Answers. `GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/ai-answers`

List AI answers generated in a conversation.

The rating UI renders a control next to a *message*, so results are also filterable by message_id — that is the key the frontend holds.

```php
$result = $sendseven->aiAnswers()->listConversation(conversationId: 'conversation_id');
```

- Scopes: `conversations:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$conversationId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$messageId` | `?string` | no | Only the event that produced this message |
| `$page` | `?int` | no |  |
| `$pageSize` | `?int` | no |  |

Returns `Page<AiAnswerEvent>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/AI%20Answers/list_conversation_ai_answers_api_v1_conversations__conversation_id__ai_answers_get)

## list

List Api Tokens. `GET /api-tokens`

List all API tokens for current user in this tenant.

By default, only shows active (non-expired, non-revoked) tokens. Set include_inactive=true to see all tokens.

```php
$result = $sendseven->apiTokens()->list();
```

| `$pageSize` | `?int` | no | Items per page |

Returns `Page<ApiToken>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/API%20Tokens/list_api_tokens_api_v1_api_tokens_get)

## create

Create Api Token. `POST /api-tokens`

Create a new API token.

IMPORTANT: The plaintext token is returned ONLY ONCE. Save it securely - you won't be able to retrieve it again.

```php
$result = $sendseven->apiTokens()->create(name: 'name', scopes: []);
```

- Scopes: `api:create`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` | yes | Human-readable name for this token |
| `$scopes` | `list<string>` | yes | Scopes granted to this token (must be subset of user's scopes) |
| `$expiresInDays` | `?int` | no | Token expiration in days (default: 90) |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `ApiTokenCreated`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/API%20Tokens/create_api_token_api_v1_api_tokens_post)

## availableScopes

Get Available Scopes For Token. `GET /api-tokens/available-scopes`

Get all scopes that the current user can grant to API tokens.

This endpoint expands wildcard scopes (*:*, resource:*, etc.) to show all granular scopes the user can select when creating tokens.

```php
$result = $sendseven->apiTokens()->availableScopes();
```

- Scopes: `api:read`

Returns `AvailableTokenScopes`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/API%20Tokens/get_available_scopes_for_token_api_v1_api_tokens_available_scopes_get)

## revoke

This permanently deletes the token. Alternatively, use PATCH to set is_active=false to soft-revoke.

| `$isEnabled` | `?bool` | no |  |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AlertDestination`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Alerts/create_alert_destination_api_v1_alert_settings_destinations_post)

## sendDestinationVerification

Send Destination Verification. `POST /alert-settings/destinations/{destination_id}/send-verification`

Send a one-time code to the destination via ITS OWN channel (SMS / WhatsApp / email). Verifying through the same channel doubles as the consent record for utility messages (plan §6.3) — verified_at is only stamped after the code round-trips against the SAME target value (security review #1: the code is bound to the phone/email, not the row).

Abuse limits (#2): per-destination hourly + per-tenant daily send quotas.

```php
$sendseven->alerts()->sendDestinationVerification(destinationId: 'destination_id');
```

- Scopes: `alerts:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$destinationId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `void`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Alerts/send_destination_verification_api_v1_alert_settings_destinations__destination_id__send_verification_post)

## deleteSettingsOverride

Delete Alert Settings Override. `DELETE /alert-settings/override`

Remove this tenant's override — it reverts to the BA default.

Tenant-scoped destination rows are kept (inert while no override exists) so re-enabling the override restores them.

```php
$sendseven->alerts()->deleteSettingsOverride();
```

- Scopes: `alerts:update`

Returns `void`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Alerts/delete_alert_settings_override_api_v1_alert_settings_override_delete)

## sendTest

Send Test Alert. `POST /alert-settings/test`

Send a test alert through the normal dispatch path.

Founder decision #10: test alerts on paid channels are billed like real sends. Throttled (security review #3/#8) and the free-text message is dropped in favour of a fixed body (security review #12 — customer text must not ride our WABA template / Slack markdown).

```php
$result = $sendseven->alerts()->sendTest();
```

- Scopes: `alerts:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$message` | `?string` | no | Optional text shown in the test alert. |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `TestAlert`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Alerts/send_test_alert_api_v1_alert_settings_test_post)

## getCampaignPerformance

Get Campaign Performance. `GET /analytics/campaigns/performance`

Get campaign performance analytics.

Returns: - Aggregate campaign stats (total/completed, sent/delivered/read/failed). Volume tiles are invoiced-aligned: non-email campaigns from campaign_messages + email campaigns from email_campaigns. - Delivery and read rates - Email breakdown (email): single/transactional (1:1, from email_messages) vs campaign/newsletter (from email_campaigns), each aligned to invoiced usage. Legacy flat email_* fields mirror email.campaign.*. - Channel-type breakdown from campaign messages - Last 5 completed campaigns


# Attachments

`$sendseven->attachments()` — 6 endpoints.

| Method | HTTP | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`createFromUrl()`](#createfromurl) | `POST /attachments/from-url` | Create Attachment From Url |
| [`upload()`](#upload) | `POST /attachments/upload` | Upload Attachment |
| [`delete()`](#delete) | `DELETE /attachments/{attachment_id}` | Delete Attachment |
| [`get()`](#get) | `GET /attachments/{attachment_id}` | Get Attachment |
| [`download()`](#download) | `GET /attachments/{attachment_id}/download` | Download Attachment |
| [`getUrl()`](#geturl) | `GET /attachments/{attachment_id}/url` | Get Attachment Url |

## createFromUrl

Create Attachment From Url. `POST /attachments/from-url`

Fetch a public URL server-side and store it as an attachment.

Returns the same shape as POST /upload so the response is interchangeable. Caller can then pass the returned id / attachment_id in MessageCreate.attachments.

```php
$result = $sendseven->attachments()->createFromUrl(url: 'url');
```

- Scopes: `messages:create`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$url` | `string` | yes | Public http(s) URL to fetch. file://, gopher://, etc. are rejected. Hostnames resolving to private/loopback/link-local IPs are blocked (SSRF protection). |
| `$filename` | `?string` | no | Optional override for the stored filename. If omitted, the filename is derived from the URL path, falling back to a UUID-based name. |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AttachmentUpload`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/create_attachment_from_url_api_v1_attachments_from_url_post)

## upload

Upload Attachment. `POST /attachments/upload`

Upload a file attachment

Args: file: The file to upload message_id: Optional message ID to associate with

```php
$result = $sendseven->attachments()->upload(file: FilePart::fromPath('/path/to/file.pdf'));
```

- Scopes: `messages:create`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$file` | `FilePart` | yes |  |
| `$messageId` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AttachmentUpload`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/upload_attachment_api_v1_attachments_upload_post)

## delete

Delete Attachment. `DELETE /attachments/{attachment_id}`

Delete an attachment

Permanently removes the attachments row and its stored blob. This is irreversible. Attachments are re-usable and carry no foreign key back to the messages that referenced them, so deleting one that a previously sent message still points at is allowed and expected — the message keeps its metadata, the media simply stops resolving.

```php
$sendseven->attachments()->delete(attachmentId: 'attachment_id');
```

- Scopes: `messages:delete`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$attachmentId` | `string` | yes |  |

Returns `void`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/delete_attachment_api_v1_attachments__attachment_id__delete)

## get

Get Attachment. `GET /attachments/{attachment_id}`

Get attachment metadata

Args: attachment_id: ID of the attachment

```php
$result = $sendseven->attachments()->get(attachmentId: 'attachment_id');
```

- Scopes: `messages:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$attachmentId` | `string` | yes |  |

Returns `AppSchemasAttachmentSchemaAttachment`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/get_attachment_api_v1_attachments__attachment_id__get)

## download

Download Attachment. `GET /attachments/{attachment_id}/download`

Download an attachment file

Args: attachment_id: ID of the attachment disposition: Content-Disposition mode - "inline" (default, for viewing in browser) or "attachment" (forces download dialog)

```php
$sendseven->attachments()->download(attachmentId: 'attachment_id');
```

- Scopes: `messages:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$attachmentId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$disposition` | `?string` | no |  |

Returns `void`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/download_attachment_api_v1_attachments__attachment_id__download_get)

## getUrl

Get Attachment Url. `GET /attachments/{attachment_id}/url`

Get a signed URL for an attachment

Args: attachment_id: ID of the attachment expiration_minutes: URL expiration time in minutes


- Scopes: `messages:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

Returns `AttachmentUrl`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Attachments/get_attachment_url_api_v1_attachments__attachment_id__url_get)

## list

List Audit Log. `GET /audit-log`

List API audit log entries for the current tenant.

Returns paginated, sanitized records of API calls made against this tenant. Sorted by most recent first.

```php
$sendseven->auditLog()->list();
```

- Scopes: `settings:admin`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$method` | `?string` | no | Filter by HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.) |
| `$statusCode` | `?int` | no | Filter by status code |
| `$path` | `?string` | no | Filter by path (partial match) |
| `$startDate` | `DateTimeInterface\|string\|null` | no | Filter from date (ISO 8601) |
| `$endDate` | `DateTimeInterface\|string\|null` | no | Filter to date (ISO 8601) |
| `$page` | `?int` | no | Page number |
| `$pageSize` | `?int` | no | Items per page |

Returns `void`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Audit%20Log/list_audit_log_api_v1_audit_log_get)

## createBot

Create Bot. `POST /automation/bots`

Create a new automation bot.

Create an AI-powered bot that can handle customer conversations using the knowledge base. Configure personality, escalation rules, and field collection requirements.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->createBot(name: 'name');
```

- Scopes: `automation:create`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` | yes | Bot display name |
| `$botType` | `BotTypeEnum\|string\|null` | no | Type of bot |
| `$isActive` | `?bool` | no | Whether bot is active |
| `$priority` | `?int` | no | Bot priority (higher = evaluated first when matching context) |
| `$personalityPrompt` | `?string` | no | Custom system prompt defining bot personality |
| `$greetingMessage` | `?string` | no | Initial greeting sent to users |
| `$escalationKeywords` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Keywords that trigger escalation (e.g., ['agent', 'human', 'help']) |
| `$displayName` | `?string` | no | Customer-facing name shown to end users (e.g., 'Eva', 'Max'). Falls back to bot name. |
| `$avatarUrl` | `?string` | no | Avatar image URL for the bot |
| `$aiDisclosureMessage` | `?string` | no | Custom AI disclosure override. Use {name} as placeholder for bot display name. |
| `$aiDisclosureIncludeEscalation` | `?bool` | no | Include 'ask for human agent' mention in the AI disclosure |
| `$isKbOnlyMode` | `?bool` | no | Only answer from knowledge base, no general knowledge |
| `$responseLanguage` | `?string` | no | ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., 'en', 'de'). null = follow the customer's language (auto-detect); ''/'auto' are stored as null. |
| `$confidenceThreshold` | `float\|int\|null` | no | Minimum confidence score to provide answer (0.0-1.0) |
| `$isDetailedResponse` | `?bool` | no | Allow longer, more detailed bot responses instead of concise chat-style messages |
| `$useFullConversationContext` | `?bool` | no | Feed the full current conversation (bounded) into the KB query instead of only the last few messages. Single-conversation only. |
| `$visionEnabled` | `?bool` | no | Beta: let the bot read images customers send (NULL/false = off). |
| `$webSearchMode` | `WebSearchModeEnum\|string\|null` | no | Beta: live web-search trigger mode — 'off' (default/NULL), 'kb_fallback' (search only after KB returns no answer), or 'always'. Any other value is rejected 422. |
| `$webSearchAllowedDomains` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Beta: restrict web search to these plain domains (injected as site: operators). Empty list = no restriction; NULL = off. Entries must be plain hosts (no scheme/path); normalized on write. |
| `$webSearchRequiredKeywords` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Beta: keywords appended to every web-search query (e.g. brand name). |
| `$webSearchMaxPerConversation` | `?int` | no | Beta: per-conversation cap on web searches (>=0). NULL = default cap. |
| `$deepAnswersEnabled` | `?bool` | no | Beta: allow deeper KB+web synthesis / reasoning bump (NULL/false = off). |
| `$autoTranslateMessages` | `?bool` | no | Auto-translate greetings, buttons, and responses to user's detected language |
| `$languageDetectionStrategy` | `?string` | no | How this bot resolves the language it speaks. 'cascade' (default) resolves per conversation via the fallback chain (contact locale -> inferred channel locale -> response_language/base_language); 'fixed' always speaks base_language. Omit / null to keep the default -- NULL is stored and treated as 'cascade' by the runtime, so existing bots are unaffected. Any other value is rejected 422. |
| `$escalationEnabled` | `?bool` | no | When disabled, the bot will never escalate to a human agent regardless of confidence score |
| `$offersEscalation` | `?bool` | no | Always offer option to talk to human |
| `$maxFailedAttempts` | `?int` | no | Low-confidence responses before auto-escalation. Use 0 for bot types where escalation does not apply (e.g. keyword bots). |
| `$handoffMessage` | `?string` | no | Custom message when escalating to human agent (e.g., 'An agent will reply soon') |
| `$noAnswerMessage` | `?string` | no | Custom text sent when the knowledge base has no answer. Empty/NULL uses the built-in localized text. Must not mention a human agent -- it is also sent when escalation is disabled. |
| `$escalationOfferMessage` | `?string` | no | Custom text appended (after one blank line) offering a human agent. Empty/NULL uses the built-in localized text. |
| `$immediateHandoffThreshold` | `float\|int\|null` | no | Confidence below this triggers immediate escalation offer (0.0-1.0) |
| `$requiredFields` | `list<array<string, mixed>>\|null` | no | Fields to collect from users |
| `$routingConfig` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no | Routing configuration (required when bot_type='router') |
| `$isFieldCollectionMode` | `?bool` | no | Enable field collection mode (auto-set for lead_qualification and appointment bots) |
| `$calendlyEventTypeUri` | `?string` | no | Calendly event type URI for booking appointments |
| `$offlineEscalationBehavior` | `OfflineEscalationBehaviorEnum\|string\|null` | no | Behavior when escalation fires but no agents online (live chat): leave_message, escalate_anyway, continue_bot |
| `$offlineMessage` | `?string` | no | Custom message shown in offline scenarios (live chat) |
| `$outsideHoursMessage` | `?string` | no | Custom message for non-livechat channels outside business hours |
| `$isEscalationScheduleEnabled` | `?bool` | no | Enable time-based escalation gating |
| `$escalationTimezone` | `?string` | no | IANA timezone for escalation schedule (e.g., 'Europe/Berlin') |
| `$escalationSchedule` | `list<array<string, mixed>>\|null` | no | Time ranges when human escalation is available |
| `$maxEmailReplies` | `?int` | no | Max email replies per conversation before handing off to agents (email_support bots) |
| `$isEmailReplyMode` | `?bool` | no | When TRUE on an 'assistant' bot, the email auto-reply logic kicks in (equivalent to legacy bot_type='email_support'). Default FALSE. |
| `$coexistBotId` | `?string` | no | ID of another bot to coexist with |
| `$coexistMode` | `?string` | no | Coexistence mode: 'active_when_active' or 'active_when_inactive' |
| `$baseLanguage` | `?string` | no | Language the bot's messages are written in (ISO 639-1) |
| `$translationCache` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no | Cached translations keyed by language code |
| `$greetingButtonsEnabled` | `?bool` | no | Show 'Talk to Human' / 'Ask the bot' buttons under the greeting (NULL/false = off) |
| `$greetingHumanButtonCaption` | `?string` | no | Caption for the 'Talk to Human' button. NULL = localized default. |
| `$greetingContinueButtonCaption` | `?string` | no | Caption for the 'Ask the bot' button. NULL = localized default. |
| `$greetingContinueAckMessage` | `?string` | no | Acknowledgement message sent after the user taps 'Ask the bot'. NULL = localized default. |
| `$sourceFooterEnabled` | `?bool` | no |  |
| `$sourceFooterMode` | `?string` | no | Which sources to list: 'urls_only' or 'urls_and_kb'. NULL = column default ('urls_only'). |
| `$sourceLinkParams` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no | Per-channel query params appended to source links, keyed by channel_type with an optional 'default' key. Shape: {channel_type: {param_name: template_string}}. NULL = no decoration. |
| `$kbLiveRefreshMode` | `?string` | no | KB live-refresh mode: 'off' \| 'always_live' \| 'cached_ttl' \| 'live_once'. NULL = 'off'. |
| `$kbLiveRefreshTtlSeconds` | `?int` | no | Cache TTL in seconds, only meaningful when kb_live_refresh_mode == 'cached_ttl'. NULL = service default. |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AutomationBot`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/create_bot_api_v1_automation_bots_post)

## reorderBots

Reorder Bots. `PUT /automation/bots/reorder`

Reorder automation bots by priority.

Updates the priority of bots based on the order in the request. The first bot in the list gets the highest priority, the last gets the lowest. Higher priority bots are evaluated first when matching context.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->reorderBots(botIds: []);
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botIds` | `list<string>` | yes | List of bot IDs in desired priority order (first = highest priority) |

Returns `BotReorder`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/reorder_bots_api_v1_automation_bots_reorder_put)

## uploadBotAvatar

Upload Bot Avatar. `POST /automation/bots/{bot_id}/avatar`

Upload an avatar image for an automation bot.

Replaces any existing bot avatar. The uploaded image is stored in GCP Cloud Storage and a signed URL is saved to the bot's avatar_url field.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->uploadBotAvatar(botId: 'bot_id', file: FilePart::fromPath('/path/to/file.pdf'));
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$file` | `FilePart` | yes | Avatar image file (PNG/JPG, max 2MB) |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `AutomationBot`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/upload_bot_avatar_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__avatar_post)

## convertBotToFlowEndpoint

Convert Bot To Flow Endpoint. `POST /automation/bots/{bot_id}/convert-to-flow`

Convert a deprecated bot into an equivalent Flow.

Only router, lead_qualification and appointment bots are convertible — calling this on any other bot type returns 400.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->convertBotToFlowEndpoint(botId: 'bot_id');
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$dryRun` | `?bool` | no | When true (default false) returns the generated flow JSON without writing anything to the database. Use this from the UI to preview the conversion before committing. |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `array<array-key, mixed>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/convert_bot_to_flow_endpoint_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__convert_to_flow_post)


- Scopes: `automation:read`

## createKeywordTrigger

Create Keyword Trigger. `POST /automation/bots/{bot_id}/keyword-triggers`

Create a keyword trigger for a bot.

Creates a new keyword trigger with its response sequence. Only applicable to bots of type KEYWORD.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->createKeywordTrigger(botId: 'bot_id', keyword: 'keyword');
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$keyword` | `string` | yes | Keyword to match |
| `$matchType` | `?string` | no | Match type: 'exact' or 'contains' |
| `$channelIds` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Limit trigger to specific channel IDs. None = all channels. |
| `$priority` | `?int` | no | Trigger priority (higher = evaluated first) |
| `$isActive` | `?bool` | no | Whether this trigger is active |
| `$handoffBotId` | `?string` | no | Bot ID to hand off to after sending responses |
| `$handoverToHuman` | `?bool` | no | Escalate to human agent after sending responses. Mutually exclusive with handoff_bot_id. |
| `$flowId` | `?string` | no | Top-level 'Start Flow' action — kick off a Flow Engine run when this keyword matches, INSTEAD of sending responses or handing off. Mutually exclusive with handoff_bot_id and handover_to_human. The referenced flow must be published. |
| `$responses` | `list<array<string, mixed>>\|null` | no | Response sequence to send when keyword is matched |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `KeywordTriggerSchema`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/create_keyword_trigger_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__keyword_triggers_post)

## reorderKeywordTriggers

Reorder keyword triggers by priority.

Updates the priority of triggers based on the order in the request. The first trigger in the list gets the highest priority. Only applicable to bots of type KEYWORD.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->reorderKeywordTriggers(botId: 'bot_id', triggerIds: []);
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$triggerIds` | `list<string>` | yes | Ordered list of trigger IDs (first = highest priority) |

Returns `list<KeywordTriggerSchema>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/reorder_keyword_triggers_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__keyword_triggers_reorder_put)

## uploadKeywordTriggerMedia

Upload Keyword Trigger Media. `POST /automation/bots/{bot_id}/keyword-triggers/upload`

Upload a media file for use in keyword trigger responses.

Uploads a file to cloud storage and returns an attachment record that can be referenced by attachment_id in keyword trigger responses.

```php
$sendseven->automation()->uploadKeywordTriggerMedia(botId: 'bot_id', file: FilePart::fromPath('/path/to/file.pdf'));
```

## createActivationRule

Create Activation Rule. `POST /automation/bots/{bot_id}/rules`

Create an activation rule for a bot.

Activation rules determine when and where a bot should be activated. Rules are evaluated in priority order (highest first).

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->createActivationRule(botId: 'bot_id');
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$channelIds` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Specific channel IDs to activate for (preferred over channel_types) |
| `$channelTypes` | `list<string>\|null` | no | [DEPRECATED] Channel types to activate for. Use channel_ids instead. |
| `$widgetIds` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Specific widget IDs to activate for |
| `$isScheduleEnabled` | `?bool` | no | Enable time-based activation |
| `$timezone` | `?string` | no | IANA timezone for schedule (e.g., 'Europe/Berlin') |
| `$timeRanges` | `list<array<string, mixed>>\|null` | no | Time ranges when bot should be active |
| `$requiresNoAgentsOnline` | `?bool` | no | Only activate when no human agents are online |
| `$recipientEmailAddresses` | `list<string>\|null` | no | Only activate for emails sent TO these addresses (e.g., ['support@example.com']) |
| `$priority` | `?int` | no | Rule priority (higher = evaluated first) |
| `$isActive` | `?bool` | no | Whether rule is active |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `BotActivationRule`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/create_activation_rule_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__rules_post)

## deleteBotTranslation

Delete Bot Translation. `DELETE /automation/bots/{bot_id}/translations/{lang_code}`

Delete the cached translations for a single language from a bot.

Idempotent: removing a language that is not present still returns 200 with the (unchanged) bot. Returns 404 only when the bot itself does not exist or is not owned by the tenant.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->deleteBotTranslation(botId: 'bot_id', langCode: 'lang_code');
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$langCode` | `string` | yes |  |

Returns `AutomationBot`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/delete_bot_translation_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__translations__lang_code__delete)

## upsertBotTranslation

Upsert Bot Translation. `PUT /automation/bots/{bot_id}/translations/{lang_code}`

Insert or replace the cached translations for a single language on a bot.

The request body is the per-language translations object (the value stored at translation_cache[lang_code]); it is free-form and may contain nested structures such as routing_messages. Returns 404 only when the bot itself does not exist or is not owned by the tenant.

```php
$result = $sendseven->automation()->upsertBotTranslation(botId: 'bot_id', langCode: 'lang_code', body: []);
```

- Scopes: `automation:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$botId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$langCode` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$body` | `array<string, mixed>` | yes | The request body |

Returns `AutomationBot`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Automation/upsert_bot_translation_api_v1_automation_bots__bot_id__translations__lang_code__put)

## create

Create Campaign. `POST /campaigns`

Create a new campaign

With scheduled_at the campaign is created as scheduled and must pass the same checks as POST /campaigns/{id}/schedule: a large WhatsApp campaign on a number that is still warming up is refused with HTTP 409 warmup_acknowledgement_required unless acknowledge_warmup_warning is true, and a split plan that runs too long is refused with HTTP 422 split_plan_too_long. Nothing is created in either case.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->create(name: 'name');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:create`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$description` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$channelContent` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no |  |
| `$messageText` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$messageType` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$attachmentId` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$targetUrl` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$browserPushTitle` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$listIds` | `list<string>\|null` | no |  |
| `$channelFilter` | `list<string>\|null` | no |  |
| `$selectedChannelIds` | `list<string>\|null` | no |  |
| `$scheduledAt` | `DateTimeInterface\|string\|null` | no |  |
| `$timezone` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$sendRateLimit` | `?int` | no | Send speed in messages per minute (1-60000). Null = channel default speed. |
| `$sendBatchSize` | `?int` | no | Recipients per batch (1-1,000,000). The campaign pauses after each batch until the next batch is sent. Null = no batches. |
| `$shouldSkipDuplicates` | `?bool` | no |  |
| `$duplicateWindowHours` | `?int` | no |  |
| `$whatsAppTemplateId` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$whatsAppTemplateName` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$whatsAppTemplateLanguage` | `?string` | no |  |
| `$whatsAppTemplateVariableMapping` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no |  |
| `$sendSplitConfig` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no |  |
| `$smsOptoutLinkEnabled` | `?bool` | no |  |
| `$acknowledgeWarmupWarning` | `?bool` | no |  |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `Campaign`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/create_campaign_api_v1_campaigns_post)

## getChannelMediaSpecs

## previewSegment

Preview Segment. `POST /campaigns/preview-segment`

Preview contacts that would be included in a segment (for UI testing)


| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

## getUnsubscribeCounts

Get Campaign Unsubscribe Counts. `GET /campaigns/unsubscribe-counts`

Batch opt-out counts for the messenger campaigns INDEX page.

ONE grouped query over the contact_subscription_events ledger for the given campaign ids (tenant-scoped). Per campaign: total opt-outs, exact (link/manual — definite attribution) and estimated (keyword heuristic). Campaigns with no opt-outs are OMITTED — treat a missing id as 0.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->getUnsubscribeCounts(ids: 'ids');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$ids` | `string` | yes | Comma-separated campaign ids (max 200) |

Returns `CampaignUnsubscribeCounts`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/get_campaign_unsubscribe_counts_api_v1_campaigns_unsubscribe_counts_get)

## getPersonalizationVariables

Get Personalization Variables. `GET /campaigns/variables`

Get available personalization variables for campaign messages.

Returns a list of variable placeholders (e.g. {{contact.name}}) that can be used in campaign message text. At send time, these placeholders are automatically replaced with the recipient contact's data.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->getPersonalizationVariables();
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:read`

Returns `array<array-key, mixed>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/get_personalization_variables_api_v1_campaigns_variables_get)

## delete

Delete Campaign. `DELETE /campaigns/{campaign_id}`

Delete a campaign (draft or scheduled only).

A campaign that has already sent messages (for example contacts enrolled from HubSpot) cannot be deleted: HTTP 400. Sent emails of an email campaign are kept for billing before the delete.

```php
$sendseven->campaigns()->delete(campaignId: 'campaign_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:delete`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$campaignId` | `string` | yes |  |

## listBatches

List Campaign Batches. `GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/batches`

Per-batch delivery counts of a campaign sent in batches

One item per batch: {batch_number, total, pending, sent, delivered, read, failed, skipped}, oldest batch first. remaining is the number of recipients waiting for a later batch, current_batch_number the batch the campaign is on and send_batch_size the saved batch size. A campaign that is not sent in batches returns an empty list.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->listBatches(campaignId: 'campaign_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:read`

## listRecipients

List Campaign Recipients. `GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/recipients`

List a campaign's recipients (messenger/newsletter) with delivery status.

Groups: successful = sent/delivered/read, failed = failed (skipped excluded), all = the union of both, held = waiting for a later batch (campaigns sent in batches; not part of all). Each item: {id, contact_id, name, identifier, status, error_reason, sent_at, delivered_at, failed_at}.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->listRecipients(campaignId: 'campaign_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:read`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$campaignId` | `string` | yes |  |

| `$page` | `?int` | no | Page number (1-indexed) |
| `$pageSize` | `?int` | no | Items per page |
| `$search` | `?string` | no | Search recipient handle, contact name or phone |

Returns `Page<CampaignRecipientItem>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/list_campaign_recipients_api_v1_campaigns__campaign_id__recipients_get)

## removeFailedRecipients

Remove Failed Campaign Recipients. `POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/recipients/remove-failed`

Bulk-remove all failed recipients from a messenger/newsletter campaign.

Hard-deletes every failed-group row for this campaign, recomputes the campaign counters and drops total_recipients by the number removed. This is DISTINCT from POST /{campaign_id}/retry-failed, which re-queues failed recipients instead of deleting them.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->removeFailedRecipients(campaignId: 'campaign_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$campaignId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `RemoveFailedRecipients`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/remove_failed_campaign_recipients_api_v1_campaigns__campaign_id__recipients_remove_failed_post)

## deleteRecipient

Delete Campaign Recipient. `DELETE /campaigns/{campaign_id}/recipients/{recipient_id}`

Remove a single recipient from a messenger/newsletter campaign.

Hard-deletes the per-recipient row (tenant + campaign ownership validated), then recomputes the campaign's denormalized counters and drops total_recipients by 1. A recipient who was already sent the message (sent / delivered / read) cannot be removed: HTTP 409.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->deleteRecipient(campaignId: 'campaign_id', recipientId: 'recipient_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

## unsubscribeRecipient

Unsubscribe Campaign Recipient. `POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/recipients/{recipient_id}/unsubscribe`

Opt a messenger/newsletter recipient's contact out of this campaign's lists.

This is DISTINCT from DELETE /{campaign_id}/recipients/{recipient_id} ("Remove"), which only deletes the per-recipient row and does NOT change subscription state. This endpoint resolves the recipient's contact, computes the campaign's originating list(s) (campaign_lists ∩ the contact's currently-subscribed lists) and opts the contact out of all of them via the subscription chokepoint, writing the opt-out ledger with campaign attribution (method='manual').

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->unsubscribeRecipient(campaignId: 'campaign_id', recipientId: 'recipient_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:update`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$campaignId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$recipientId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `RecipientUnsubscribe`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/unsubscribe_campaign_recipient_api_v1_campaigns__campaign_id__recipients__recipient_id__unsubscribe_post)

## resume

Resume Campaign. `POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/resume`

Resume a paused or failed campaign

For split-sending campaigns the remaining recipients are re-planned from now: today's batch is sent, later batches continue on the following days.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->resume(campaignId: 'campaign_id');
```

## retryFailedRecipients

Retry Failed Recipients. `POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/retry-failed`

Retry failed recipients of a campaign

Resets FAILED recipients back to pending and re-queues them for sending. Designed for "top up, then retry": an SMS campaign that was paused because the prepaid SMS balance was used up can be re-driven with {"error_codes": ["insufficient_sms_balance"]} once credit is available. SMS recipients the carrier rejected or did not deliver are re-driven with {"error_codes": ["sms_rejected_by_carrier"]} / ["sms_not_delivered"] (e.g. after the cause of an automatic pause was fixed). SMS recipients that failed because the SMS provider temporarily limited the sending rate are re-driven with {"error_codes": ["sms_rate_limited"]} -- lower the campaign's send_rate_limit or set a send_batch_size first (PUT /campaigns/{id}) so the retry does not hit the limit again. With no body (or an empty list) every failed recipient is retried. Unknown codes return HTTP 422 listing the allowed codes.

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->retryFailedRecipients(campaignId: 'campaign_id');
```

- Scopes: `campaigns:send`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$campaignId` | `string` | yes |  |
| `$body` | `array<string, mixed>\|null` | no | The request body |
| `$idempotencyKey` | `?string` | no | Repeat a request safely: SendSeven answers a repeat with the first result. One is generated when omitted. |

Returns `array<array-key, mixed>`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/retry_failed_recipients_api_v1_campaigns__campaign_id__retry_failed_post)

```php
$result = $sendseven->campaigns()->schedule(campaignId: 'campaign_id', scheduledAt: 'scheduled_at', timezone: 'timezone');
```

Returns `Campaign`. [SendSeven reference](https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/docs#/Campaigns/schedule_campaign_api_v1_campaigns__campaign_id__schedule_post)
